This documents the traditional explanation, not independent proof that the graph was historically assembled from separate semantic parts.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected received Shuowen text and annotation and an opened Chinese CText dictionary aggregation. These support the traditional account and list citations/readings, but do not provide a verified earliest inscription context or semantic chronology.

gaps: No visually inspected early oracle-bone or bronze glyph pixels or primary inscription context establishes the earliest lexical sense of 高; catalogued categories and broad descriptions do not supply a dated semantic chain.

Early form descriptions support a tall pavilion/building interpretation, but specific architectural details, graphic transitions, or scribal corruption cannot be established from the inspected rendered pages.
The received Shuowen segmentation into 冂、口 remains a historical lexicographic account; separate original semantic contributions are unproven.
The supplied Shuowen Seal Radical 187 file lead could not be opened either as a Commons page or through the attempted imageinfo API. Its graph identity and reuse terms remain unknown.
No local 京 reading records were repeated as a sound comparison because no phonetic component is proposed; resemblance to 京 is not evidence of shared ancestry or borrowing.

The exact onset and chronology of extensions such as excellence, esteem, high price, old age, and loud/forceful voice remain unresolved; dictionary gloss and citation order cannot establish semantic chronology.

No high-vs-tall lexical sound loan or other whole-graph borrowing claim is advanced. The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan connection and possible lexical links to 喬 or 浩 remain unsubstantiated by the inspected sources.
